the inclusion of chemical potentials, which are bound to arise due the separation of chemical from kinetic freeze-out, can reduce the value of the shear viscosity to entropy ratio and thus make hydrodynamic simulations of heavy-ion collisions at RHIC successful, even if the shear viscosity to temperature ratio is not close to the lower string-theory bound throughout the collision evolution.

a pion chemical potential is bound to arise during the evolution of the system, that this chemical potential reduces the shear viscosity, and that this reduction is enough to allow for a successful description of the experimental data by viscous hydrodynamics.

the inclusion of chemical potentials is essential for a consistent treatment of the evolution of the system.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the extraction of η/s from the experimental data requires careful consideration of the chemical composition of the system.
the value of η/ s extracted from microscopic transport simulations is strongly dependent on the chemical potentials present in the hadron gas, which are often neglected in the analysis of the data.
